purpose: Compare the remaining twelve App prayers linked to Holy See 2005 Compendium English/French/Latin published sections, without changing canonical texts.

sourceWitnesses.latin: Printed Latin parallels embedded in both official English and French documents

languageFindings.en: The app uses 'is seated'/'from there', while the English Compendium prints 'sits'/'from thence'. Same apostolic articles, different translation choices.
languageFindings.fr: The app uses 'Je crois au Saint-Esprit' whereas the printed French Creed has 'Je crois en l’Esprit Saint'; do not treat this as word-for-word collation.
languageFindings.la: The same Symbolum Apostolicum is present, with accentuation and punctuation differences; independent character-level collation remains open.

items.editorialNext: Lock the approved traditional vernacular Creed witness and determine canonical spelling, not substitute the 2005 phrasing.

languageFindings.en: The English penitential formula substantially agrees with the Compendium, including the near occasion of sin; capitalization and punctuation differ.
languageFindings.fr: The app follows the printed French act's wording but adds 'Amen' after 'faire pénitence'; that French Amen is not printed before the next act heading.
languageFindings.la: The Latin Actus contritionis aligns in substance; accents/ligatures and punctuation differ.

items.editorialNext: Record whether the app's final French Amen is a separately authorized customary conclusion; no silent deletion.

languageFindings.en: The English Act of Faith follows the Compendium text and closing formula in substance.
languageFindings.fr: The same short French act, including 'Dans cette foi', appears in the official French appendix.
languageFindings.la: The Latin Actus fidei is present in its corresponding edition; diacritic and punctuation differences remain.

items.editorialNext: Normalize only authorized typography; full three-language exact-text proofreading remains open.

languageFindings.en: English closing says 'In this hope' as the app does.
languageFindings.fr: The Vatican's printed French Acte d’espérance actually ends 'Dans cette foi', and the app retains this unusual printed wording. Do NOT silently change to 'espérance'.
languageFindings.la: The Latin source says 'In hac spe', retained by the app; the French and Latin differ at the closing even within the same published edition.

items.editorialNext: Cross-check an earlier printed French catechism edition and retain exact official 2005 variant attribution.

languageFindings.en: The app matches the English theological act and its closing in substance.
languageFindings.fr: The Compendium French Acte de charité ends after 'pour l’amour de vous', with no extra English-style closing; the app likewise does not append it.
languageFindings.la: The printed Latin Actus caritatis contains the closing 'In hac caritate' and Amen, as the app does.

items.editorialNext: Perform literal punctuation/orthography audit for en/fr/la and record the intentional different-length French edition.

languageFindings.en: The Compendium prints the same rhyming 'Angel of God' prayer and Amen.
languageFindings.fr: French Ange de Dieu substantially matches the printed lines; punctuation is not yet certified.
languageFindings.la: Latin Angele Dei corresponds in all petitions; accents and spelling are normalization differences.

items.editorialNext: Collate original line breaks and typography for all three languages.

languageFindings.en: The app's archaic 'thee/thine' style relates to the UK form, whereas the Compendium also offers a different US vernacular; the app appends an ℣/℟ response after the antiphon.
languageFindings.fr: The app is a traditional vouvoiement form ('Vers vous', 'Ô vous') whereas the French Compendium prints tutoiement ('Vers toi', 'Ô toi').
languageFindings.la: The core Salve Regina matches the Latin antiphon, but the app appends Ora pro nobis / Ut digni versus absent from the printed Salve antiphon unit.

items.editorialNext: Give the antiphon and appended versicle independent source IDs and historical edition witnesses before publication as a single witness.

languageFindings.en: The English Memorare is broadly aligned with the Compendium prayer; punctuation differs.
languageFindings.fr: The French text is a substantive traditional variant: the app has 'réclamé votre intercession' versus 'réclamé votre secours', and 'Mère du Verbe incarné' versus 'Mère du Verbe' in the 2005 source.
languageFindings.la: Latin Memorare substantially agrees; spelling/accents and punctuation vary.

items.editorialNext: Find a printed pre-1962 French Memorare witness for the app's exact traditional wording; no automatic Compendium overwrite.

languageFindings.en: The app's English text follows the Compendium USA VERSION (not UK VERSION) and includes its doxology.
languageFindings.fr: The app uses related contemporary French Magnificat wording but not the exact Compendium text ('Sa miséricorde' versus 'Son amour', and alternate descendants phrasing); its doxology is absent.
languageFindings.la: The app prints the Magnificat canticle but omits the concluding Gloria Patri that the Latin Compendium appends.

items.editorialNext: Split canticle and doxology as source-scoped optional components and collate the French source edition; do not auto-append liturgical elements without mode evidence.

languageFindings.en: The app uses a prose/literal Anima Christi ('sanctify me'; 'wash me') while the Compendium EN prints a substantially different rhymed translation ('be my sanctification'; 'wash out my stains').
languageFindings.fr: The app is close to the Compendium's French rendering, but has 'Dans tes plaies' versus printed 'Dans tes blessures'; punctuation also differs.
languageFindings.la: The app follows the traditional Latin Anima Christi; accents, ligatures and minor punctuation are not fully collated.

items.editorialNext: Retain traditional prose English; locate primary printed witnesses for exact English and French variants, without treating the rhymed 2005 text as equivalent.

languageFindings.en: The app follows the Compendium USA VERSION in substance, including its Gloria Patri conclusion; it does not use the UK VERSION.
languageFindings.fr: The app's French canticle is close to the 2005 printed version but omits its different closing doxology ('Gloire au Père ... au Dieu qui est').
languageFindings.la: The app's Latin canticle omits the Gloria Patri conclusion printed after the Benedictus by the Compendium.

items.editorialNext: Specify when Gloria Patri is supplied by the Divine Office/liturgy versus included inside a standalone Benedictus reader.

languageFindings.en: English Eternal Rest substantially matches the Compendium text.
languageFindings.fr: Substantive difference: app asks that 'la lumière éternelle brille sur eux'; French Compendium instead asks that 'brille sur eux la lumière de ta face'.
languageFindings.la: Traditional Latin Requiem aeternam and Requiescant in pace substantially match, with accentuation differences.

items.editorialNext: Find a pinned traditional French Requiem translation supporting 'lumière éternelle'; do not impose the 2005 alternative.
